findings.title: 质控启动绑定不核对已有项目关联，缺失保护登记仍可报告就绪
findings.confidence: high: no startup traversal or reconciliation exists in inspected implementation
findings.evidence: initialize validates/generates the local dataset_uuid and emits ready. bindCatalog checks only catalog schema, reservation table presence and foreign_keys, then emits catalogBound. Neither scans quality_item_proj/qc_project_snapshot/quality_data nor checks expected holds or own-dataset orphan holds. load reads local data only. shell/main.cpp accepts catalogBound plus ordinary load as readiness. ProjectsStore rename/delete protection consults the catalog reservation rows, not QcStore::inspectProjectReference.
trigger_inputs: A valid tagged quality_control.db with a persistent UUID and existing association control C -> project P; pair it with a restored catalog whose schema and P ID/name still match but whose quality_control reservation K is absent.
Reopen QcStore, bind that catalog, set its committed candidate list and load. All current startup checks succeed without re-establishing K.
Use real ProjectsStore to rename P; use a nonfixed project with no other catalog references to test deletion. Missing K provides no protection for the saved QC association/name history.
Conversely, a reservation left after successful local deletion and failed release is neither diagnosed as orphan nor given a recovery state during the next bind.
findings.impact: After restore, partial failure or explicit hold removal, saved QC rows/history can reference a project that the catalog is allowed to rename/delete. This breaks the advertised durable identity protection; normal successful CRUD tests do not establish recovery coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Under the same dataset writer-serialization protocol as association writes, enumerate all saved associations, including controls with is_used=0, validate stable ID/name and historical snapshots, reserve missing expected keys and diagnose own-dataset orphan/conflicting keys before declaring reference readiness. quality_data has string identity: historical names that cannot be resolved through a valid saved association must fail closed for explicit reconciliation, not be guessed. Keep historical units/ratios/decimals; do not compare them blindly to current project presentation or auto-delete orphan holds.
findings.suggested_verification: Real ProjectsStore/ReagentStore fixture: missing hold after restore, matching stable UUID reopen, invalid/missing/renamed project, inactive control with history, orphan hold, catalog lock and reserve-commit failure. Check no ready/catalogBound success until protection is reconciled, and unchanged QC rows/history on failure.
findings.runtime_status: not run; deterministic recovery scenario derived from source

findings.title: 同一质控数据集的并发保存/解除关联可释放另一写者正在使用的保护登记
findings.confidence: high: source explicitly commits catalog reservation before local BEGIN and releases keys outside a local writer lock
findings.evidence: setProjects reserves/commits catalog holds at486 and only then obtains local BEGIN IMMEDIATE at487. Failed begin/write/commit rolls back the local transaction before releaseReferences(newKeys). Successful association removal commits local deletion before releaseReferences(removedKeys). The key is dataset UUID + control ID + project ID, so two QcStore connections to the same local file intentionally share a key. Calibration's existing same-dataset ABORT test does not cover these QC paths.
trigger_interleaving_normal_success: Begin with C associated with P and durable hold K.
Writer A setProjects(C,{}) commits local removal, pause immediately before line537 releases K.
Writer B setProjects(C,{P}) sees K already present, so newKeys is empty; B commits the newly added local association.
A resumes releaseReferences(K). Both calls report success, but B's committed association is now unprotected.
trigger_interleaving_failure: A reserves a new K then pauses before obtaining the local writer lock, or encounters a write failure and rolls back before cleanup.
B reuses that existing K and commits the same association while A has no local writer lock.
A releases its remembered newKeys, deleting K now required by B.
findings.impact: A real saved association can lose rename/delete protection with no failed final operation. A mutex on one QObject or one GUI busy flag does not serialize another store/process using the same dataset.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one cross-connection/process dataset operation-serialization policy with a consistent local->catalog lock order. Acquire the local writer lock before new reservation, and retain serialization through failed-action cleanup. For post-commit detach cleanup, reacquire the local writer lock, recheck that the association is still absent and release the catalog key while that check is protected; or use an operation lock spanning both file commits. If safe absence cannot be established, keep the conservative hold and surface reconciliation. Preserve other datasets/owners and never release pre-existing keys as a shortcut.
findings.suggested_verification: Two real QcStore instances on the same quality_control.db with deterministic test barriers around reservation/local commit/cleanup. Cover both successful detach-versus-reattach and failed-add-versus-successful-add, and assert every persisted association retains the appropriate hold. No scheduling-only timing claim.
findings.runtime_status: not run; concrete legal interleaving derived from current statements

findings.title: 校准失败回收依赖本地事务仍持锁，自动回滚故障没有对应保护
findings.confidence: conditional: the existing ABORT failure path is protected; the proposed ROLLBACK path has not been run
findings.evidence: On writeRecord or COMMIT error, save/copy call cleanupFailedReferences assuming the local BEGIN IMMEDIATE is still active, then call rollback. There is no transaction-state/operation-lock check before destructive cleanup. tests/calibration_reference_test.cpp::sameDatasetConcurrentFailureCannotReleaseCommittedHold uses RAISE(ABORT), which keeps the enclosing transaction active and therefore verifies that narrower case.
trigger_inputs: Use a controlled fixture trigger on calibration_points for blood_batch='FAIL': BEFORE INSERT ... BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ROLLBACK,'forced automatic rollback'); END.
Writer A first commits newly acquired project/batch holds, then its point insert executes the trigger; the local transaction and its lock end as part of the error.
Before A's cleanup transaction, writer B on the same local dataset begins, reuses the existing pair holds and commits a valid record.
A's remembered newProjects/newBatches cleanup can delete holds required by B. Relevant storage errors may also end a transaction; this review does not claim those error classes were reproduced.
findings.impact: The comment that the local write lock is still held is an assumption, rather than a protected invariant for every error path. The usual ABORT/BUSY recovery and already-tested normal concurrency remain sound under their stated lock assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Before releasing new holds after a local error, establish that dataset serialization is still held. If a transaction may have auto-rolled back, reacquire the local writer lock and check actual persisted pair identities before releasing; otherwise keep the conservative holds for explicit startup reconciliation. An operation lock spanning both connections is another option. Do not unconditionally clear all owner/dataset holds.
findings.suggested_verification: Add a deterministic same-dataset two-writer RAISE(ROLLBACK) test separately from the existing RAISE(ABORT) test. Include one failed cleanup/lock case and assert an explicit retained-hold diagnostic. This is a proposed test, not an executed result.
findings.runtime_status: not run; targeted exception-path test proposal based on the current lock assumption

findings.title: 质控保护登记释放失败的警告会被后续普通读取成功覆盖
findings.confidence: high: same worker emits warning then succeeded; page reload subsequently replaces status with normal success
trigger_inputs: Commit a QC control/association deletion, then make the catalog unavailable/locked during releaseReferences so release fails.

Store emits warning and then succeeded because local deletion is real. Page warning handler only reports status; succeeded queues reload. snapshotReady reports ordinary data-read success and operationFinished(true).

The remaining orphan hold blocks future project mutation, but the final business status no longer explains why reconciliation is still required. The process log retains a warning; no persistent page recovery state or retry entry is exposed.
findings.impact: Data is conservatively protected, but users can be left with an apparently complete operation and a later inexplicable project-lock error. This is recovery/observability, not a claim that the local deletion should be falsely rolled back or reported unsaved.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a pending-reference-reconciliation condition and affected stable keys in storage-facing state, preserve a plain-language notice across routine reloads, and provide a safe retry/reconcile action that rechecks local absence. Keep local commit success distinct from reference-cleanup completion. Startup reconciliation from IRR-01 should expose the same condition.
findings.runtime_status: not run; signal-order and handler behavior inspected statically

confirmed_contracts.topic: 校准数据集身份与启动对账
confirmed_contracts.conclusion: Known v3 local library appends dataset_uuid/reference_protocol only when both values are absent; partial/invalid identities fail closed. Startup scans DISTINCT identity tuples without visible=1 or the 2048-page limit, protects hidden history, and rejects own-dataset orphan holds without automatically deleting them. Local writer lock precedes catalog lock in the normal reconciliation path.

confirmed_contracts.topic: 校准两库提交的正常顺序
confirmed_contracts.conclusion: For normal active local transactions, reserve project and optional batch in catalog, commit catalog holds, then commit local record/points. Cleanup targets only keys newly inserted by that action; existing holds and other owners/datasets are untouched. A failed cleanup retains conservative protection and contextual error text. No cross-file foreign key or single atomic transaction is claimed. IRR-03 scopes the remaining exceptional assumption.

Delete changes visible=0 with revision check and leaves record/point identity plus holds intact. It does not delete historic points or free a hold just because the row disappeared from the visible list.

Project keys are project_base.id; batch keys are reagent_batch_group.id. QC key includes dataset/control/project; calibration key includes dataset/project/batch. Owners quality_control and calibration are separate. Original/Calibration/Rate/INR are explicit text-to-enum mappings; unknown Time is not guessed as Original. batchId=0 creates no batch hold, rather than implying default/apply. QC control batches are not reagent batch IDs.

confirmed_contracts.topic: 保存时的单位/倍率/精度快照
confirmed_contracts.conclusion: QC snapshot stores result name/type/unit/ratio/decimals at association creation and existing association retention does not replace it with current presentation. Calibration stores raw point values and concentration/result unit plus ratio as provenance; saved identity update/copy preserves them without applying conversion. New calibration records check current units/ratio and Original/Calibration existence; historical writes/copy still require dictionary units/type identity, while disabled projects are allowed for startup read/protection only. Calibration has no per-result decimal snapshot field; its raw input max4-decimal contract is separate and should not be advertised as current project display precision.

confirmed_contracts.topic: 角色来源和未启用动作
confirmed_contracts.conclusion: Current CalibrationStore checks authenticated/actionReady roles1..5 on writes, and the shell propagates its account session through CalibrationPage; this preserves the previously accepted migrated baseline. QC has no AccountSession gate and current shell tests explicitly leave its local editor available for all six roles; inspected original QC manager/chooser/main navigation source shows no corresponding role guard. Do not invent an Engineer restriction during reference repair. Original calibration apply/default-apply Engineer/UserPower guards concern disabled clinical actions, not proof of exact local raw-edit role equivalence. Full original active-Windows role behavior remains a separate pending comparison.

confirmed_contracts.topic: 共用目录结构所有权与SQL线程
confirmed_contracts.conclusion: QC/calibration consume, rather than create, the catalog reservation schemas. SQL handles/connections are created and used in the owning store thread; no QWidget/GUI SQL connection is passed to them. Calibration initialization follows reagent/sample readiness, so required catalog reservation tables have already been committed.

Reagent success callback matches real save/remove operation names after catalog commit and triggers project reload only when ready, not busy and without unsaved changes. Re-entering project page refreshes again under the same guards. Only committed snapshots feed downstream choices; project drafts are not substituted for them. Requests are filtered and controls made busy during reload. No draft-clobber finding was established in this callback.

QC numeric rule validation now uses \z, with range/max4-decimal checks. The previously discussed trailing-newline acceptance is absent from this inspected validator; this review does not count it as an open bug.

explicit_assumptions_and_followups: Each persistent dataset UUID is assumed to identify one actively shared local database file. Copying a library byte-for-byte to another independently active directory preserves UUID but loses the common local lock. Neither reviewed store enforces a one-active-file rule for cloned UUIDs. Document/reject concurrent divergent clones or add a shared dataset-level operation lock before claiming protection for that deployment; no such clone test was run here.

Busy/dirty-skipped candidate refresh is not queued as a pending invalidation; the next project-page entry refreshes it. An external catalog writer can therefore leave displayed candidates stale until refresh. Store-side reference checks still reject stale invalid save data. This is a freshness limit, not established silent data corruption in the inspected unified flow.

Original Windows behavior, real screen and protocol/clinical effectiveness are outside this static review. Old history must continue to use its saved values/units/precision, not current catalog formatting.
